title: Ghosts, Ouija boards and ESP: psychology and the paranormal, with Chris French, PhD

sentences.en: It's almost Halloween, time for kids of all ages to dress up as ghosts and monsters, watch scary movies, and indulge in all things spooky and supernatural.
sentences.zh: 万圣节快到了，这是所有年龄段的孩子们装扮成鬼怪、观看恐怖电影、沉浸在各种诡异和超自然事物中的时刻。

sentences.en: The costumes and treats are just for fun, but surveys suggest that many people take ghosts quite seriously.
sentences.zh: 服装和糖果只是为了好玩，但调查显示，许多人确实非常认真地看待鬼魂。

sentences.en: One 2019 poll found that 20% of Americans believe that ghosts definitely exist, and another 25% say they probably exiSt.
sentences.zh: 2019年的一项民意调查发现，20%的美国人认为鬼魂确实存在，另有25%的人表示它们可能存在。

sentences.en: Many others believe in extrasensory perception, demons, space alien abduction, near-death experiences, and all sorts of unearthly things.
sentences.zh: 还有许多人相信超感官知觉、恶魔、外星人绑架、濒死体验以及各种各样的超自然事物。

sentences.en: Where do these beliefs come from?
sentences.zh: 这些信仰从何而来？

sentences.en: What is behind their enduring appeal?
sentences.zh: 它们持久吸引力的背后是什么？

sentences.en: And what explanations, psychological rather than supernatural, might underlie paranormal experiences?
sentences.zh: 除了超自然解释之外，还有哪些心理学解释可能构成超自然体验的基础？

sentences.en: What does the science tell us?
sentences.zh: 科学告诉我们什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Chris French, an emeritus professor of psychology and head of the Anomalistic Psychology Research Unit at Goldsmiths University of London.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是克里斯·弗伦奇博士，他是伦敦大学金史密斯学院心理学名誉教授，也是异常心理学研究部门的负责人。

sentences.en: He studies the psychology of paranormal beliefs and anomalous experiences, looking for psychological explanations for phenomena including near-death experiences, ESP,
sentences.zh: 他研究超自然信仰和异常体验的心理学，为包括濒死体验、超感官知觉在内的现象寻找心理学解释，

sentences.en: and ghostly visitations, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如鬼魂造访等。

sentences.en: He's written more than 150 journal articles and book chapters and several scholarly books.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了150多篇期刊文章和书籍章节，以及几本学术著作。

sentences.en: He also brings his research to the public by writing regular columns for the UK publications Skeptic and The Guardian, and he makes frequent appearances on TV, radio,
sentences.zh: 他还通过为英国出版物《怀疑论者》和《卫报》撰写定期专栏，将他的研究带给公众，并经常出现在电视、广播、

sentences.en: and podcasts to offer a skeptic's perspective on paranormal experiences.
sentences.zh: 以及播客中，从怀疑论者的角度对超自然体验提供见解。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. French.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，弗伦奇博士。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: So I just mentioned that you're the head of the Anomalistic Psychology Research Unit at the University of London.
sentences.zh: 我刚才提到您是伦敦大学异常心理学研究部门的负责人。

sentences.en: What is anomalistic psychology?
sentences.zh: 什么是异常心理学？

sentences.en: Yeah, I thought that might be the first question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这可能是第一个问题。

sentences.en: Anomalistic psychology is primarily focused upon trying to come up with, and where possible put to the test, non-paranormal explanations, usually psychological explanations,
sentences.zh: 异常心理学主要致力于尝试提出——并在可能的情况下进行测试——非超自然的解释，通常是心理学解释，

sentences.en: for ostensibly paranormal experiences.
sentences.zh: 来解释表面上看起来是超自然的体验。

sentences.en: So all the kinds of things you just mentioned there, people who think they've been abducted by aliens,
sentences.zh: 所以，你刚才提到的所有那些事情，比如那些认为自己被外星人绑架的人，

sentences.en: people who think they've seen ghosts or that they have psychic powers and so on, are a kind of working hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 那些认为自己见过鬼魂或拥有通灵能力的人等等，都是一种工作假设。

sentences.en: And I have to emphasize, this is all it is, but it's a working hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 我必须强调，这仅仅是一个工作假设。

sentences.en: Let's assume paranormal forces don't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 让我们假设超自然力量并不存在。

sentences.en: Can we explain those claims in other terms?
sentences.zh: 我们能用其他术语来解释这些主张吗？

sentences.en: I would self-identify as a skeptic, certainly.
sentences.zh: 我当然会自认为是怀疑论者。

sentences.en: But for me, an important part of skepticism is to always be open to the possibility that you might be wrong.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，怀疑论的一个重要部分是始终对你可能是错的这种可能性保持开放态度。

sentences.en: New evidence might come along that makes you revise your opinion.
sentences.zh: 新的证据可能会出现，让你修正自己的观点。

sentences.en: For the time being, I would have to say, I don't believe that paranormal forces exiSt.
sentences.zh: 目前，我不得不说，我不相信超自然力量存在。

sentences.en: So what are some of the psychological or cognitive factors that drive belief in the supernatural?
sentences.zh: 那么，推动人们相信超自然现象的心理或认知因素有哪些呢？

sentences.en: People are very wedded to these beliefs.
sentences.zh: 人们对这些信仰非常执着。

sentences.en: I think there's a whole host of different kinds of cognitive biases and weird experiences that people genuinely do have.
sentences.zh: 我认为这背后有一整套不同的认知偏差和人们确实会有的奇怪体验。

sentences.en: I retired about a year ago, but before that, I used to teach a 20-hour course on this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我大约一年前退休了，但在那之前，我经常教授一门关于这些内容的20小时课程。

sentences.en: So we'll try and boil it down into around 40 minutes or so.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试着把它浓缩到40分钟左右。

sentences.en: But basically, people do have genuinely weird experiences.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，人们确实会有真正奇怪的体验。

sentences.en: Just to give one example, one of the ones that we're most interested in is a phenomenon called sleep paralysis, which is fairly common in its most basic form.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我们最感兴趣的现象之一叫做睡眠瘫痪症，它在最基本的形式下是相当普遍的。

sentences.en: But for a few people, they get very, very vivid hallucinations while they're having this experience as they lie there in their bed.
sentences.zh: 但对少数人来说，当他们躺在床上经历这种体验时，会出现非常非常生动的幻觉。

sentences.en: And if you already believe in ghosts or demons and so on, it's not surprising that they will sometimes opt for that as an explanation.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经相信鬼魂或恶魔之类的东西，那么他们有时会选择这种解释也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: So that's just one example.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个例子。

sentences.en: There's a whole range of cognitive biases that are also relevant to this topic.
sentences.zh: 还有一系列与此主题相关的认知偏差。

sentences.en: Again, just to give you a couple of examples,
sentences.zh: 同样，仅举几个例子，

sentences.en: because the very first systematic investigation of the unreliability of eyewitness testimony was actually carried out in the context of a faked seance back in the Victorian era.
sentences.zh: 因为对目击证词不可靠性的第一次系统性调查，实际上是在维多利亚时代一场伪造的降神会背景下进行的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, again, a lot of paranormal claims are based on anecdotal evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，很多超自然的主张都是基于轶事证据的。

sentences.en: And we've always got that problem of, well, how reliable is the account?
sentences.zh: 我们总是面临这样一个问题：这些描述到底有多可靠？

sentences.en: Even if the person's being honest, they may be mistaken.
sentences.zh: 即使当事人是诚实的，他们也可能弄错了。

sentences.en: And then when it comes to paranormal belief, again, there are a whole host of cognitive biases, problems that we have with probabilistic reasoning, for example.
sentences.zh: 当谈到超自然信仰时，同样，存在着一整套认知偏差，例如我们在概率推理方面遇到的问题。

sentences.en: The list goes on and on, and I'm sure we can touch on some of them during our talk.
sentences.zh: 这样的例子不胜枚举，我相信我们在谈话中可以触及其中一些。

sentences.en: I thought it was particularly interesting that you studied sleep paralysis.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你研究睡眠瘫痪症特别有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something that I experienced a great deal when I was a college student.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在大学读书时经常经历这种情况。

sentences.en: And I think you've found that that's true among college students.
sentences.zh: 我想你已经发现这在大学生中很普遍。

sentences.en: And just to help people better understand, I mean, it's almost like you're conscious, but you're asleep.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助人们更好地理解，我的意思是，这几乎就像你清醒着，但又在睡觉。

sentences.en: Can you explain a little more about what's happening?
sentences.zh: 你能多解释一下发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: It is this kind of weird hybrid state between normal waking consciousness and dream consciousness.
sentences.zh: 这是一种介于正常清醒意识和梦境意识之间的奇怪混合状态。

sentences.en: And as you say, students are particularly prone to it, interestingly.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，有趣的是，学生特别容易出现这种情况。

sentences.en: In terms of what I would call kind of basic sleep paralysis, which is really when you're half awake, half asleep, and you realise you can't move.
sentences.zh: 就我所说的基本睡眠瘫痪症而言，实际上就是当你半梦半醒时，意识到自己无法动弹。

sentences.en: It's a period of temporary paralysis.
sentences.zh: 这是一个暂时瘫痪的时期。

sentences.en: And it lasts a few seconds and you snap out of it and you maybe think, that was a bit weird, but it doesn't really go any further than that.
sentences.zh: 它持续几秒钟，然后你突然清醒过来，可能会想，那有点奇怪，但并没有什么进一步的发展。

sentences.en: Interestingly, estimates vary hugely from one study to another across different countries, from literally a fraction of a percentage point up to 65%, 70%.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，不同国家的研究对这一比例的估计差异巨大，从字面上看，从不到百分之一到65%、70%不等。

sentences.en: So clearly there's something weird going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以显然那里发生了一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: And it's really about, obviously, how you ask the question, how you define it, so how you present it to people.
sentences.zh: 这显然取决于你如何提问，如何定义它，以及你如何向人们展示它。

sentences.en: But the best estimate we have, taking all those surveys into account, this is from an American friend of mine, Brian Sharpless,
sentences.zh: 但考虑到所有这些调查，我们得到的最佳估计——这是我的一位美国朋友布莱恩·夏普莱斯得出的，

sentences.en: about 8% of the population will experience sleep paralysis at least once in their life.
sentences.zh: 大约8%的人口一生中至少会经历一次睡眠瘫痪症。

sentences.en: But that's the general population.
sentences.zh: 但这只是普通人群。

sentences.en: There are two groups that stand out in terms of having rates of more like 30%, and that is students and psychiatric patients, which is kind of quite interesting.
sentences.zh: 有两个群体在发生率上显得突出，达到了30%左右，那就是学生和精神病患者，这相当有趣。

sentences.en: It does make sense, because if you have the underlying susceptibility, then you're much more likely to have an episode if your sleep pattern is disrupted.
sentences.zh: 这确实说得通，因为如果你有潜在的易感性，那么如果你的睡眠模式被打乱，你就更有可能经历发作。

sentences.en: And two groups who have notoriously irregular sleep patterns would be students and psychiatric patients.
sentences.zh: 而众所周知，睡眠模式不规律的两个群体就是学生和精神病患者。

sentences.en: Now, as I say, in its most basic form, it's no big deal.
sentences.zh: 现在，正如我所说，在最基本的形式下，这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: But for a smaller percentage of people, you can get a host of associated symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 但对于一小部分人来说，可能会出现一系列相关的症状。

sentences.en: You can get a sense of presence, feeling that there's something evil in the room with you.
sentences.zh: 你可能会有一种存在感，感觉到房间里有邪恶的东西和你在一起。

sentences.en: Even if you can't see it or hear it, you just know it's there.
sentences.zh: 即使你看不见也听不见，你就是知道它在那里。

sentences.en: But sometimes people do actually hallucinate.
sentences.zh: 但有时人们确实会产生幻觉。

sentences.en: So they might hear voices or footsteps or mechanical sounds.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会听到声音、脚步声或机械声。

sentences.en: They might see lights moving around the room or dark shadows or even demons and witches, hags, all sorts of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会看到光线在房间里移动，或者看到黑暗的阴影，甚至恶魔、女巫、老妖婆，各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And also people often report a sense of pressure on the chest, difficulty breathing.
sentences.zh: 而且人们经常报告胸部有压迫感，呼吸困难。

sentences.en: Now, I can imagine if you get all this, it's not too surprising that people also report intense fear.
sentences.zh: 现在，我可以想象，如果你经历了这一切，人们报告强烈的恐惧也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: But it's the kind of fear that's almost over and above the kind of fear that even people who in real life have been in life-threatening situations feel.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种恐惧，几乎超过了即使在现实生活中处于危及生命的情况下的人所感受到的那种恐惧。

sentences.en: They say, this is just orders of magnitude greater.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这比那要强烈得多。

sentences.en: And it's possible that it's the over-activation of the amygdala that's maybe causing that.
sentences.zh: 这可能是杏仁核过度激活导致的。

sentences.en: So it's an integral part of the whole experience.
sentences.zh: 所以这是整个体验中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: But it's absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对令人着迷。

sentences.en: I get sent lots of first-hand accounts.
sentences.zh: 我收到了很多第一手的描述。

sentences.en: And again, I'm a skeptic.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我是个怀疑论者。

sentences.en: Usually the person who's sending me the account is a skeptic because they've figured out for themselves it's sleep paralysis, this thing that we know about.
sentences.zh: 通常给我发描述的人也是怀疑论者，因为他们自己已经弄清楚了这是睡眠瘫痪症，是我们已知的东西。

sentences.en: But the stories can still send a shiver down your spine.
sentences.zh: 但这些故事仍然会让你不寒而栗。

sentences.en: I don't think my episodes were ever that entertaining.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我的经历有那么有趣。

sentences.en: Another area that you've studied is the idea motor effect, the fact that people can make movements that they're not consciously aware of.
sentences.zh: 你研究的另一个领域是意动效应，即人们可以做出他们意识不到的动作。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: And it's supposedly behind things like dousing for water or Ouija boards.
sentences.zh: 据说这背后是像寻水术或通灵板之类的东西。

sentences.en: And I found this especially interesting because when I was a kid, I was in junior high school, I had a friend.
sentences.zh: 我发现这一点特别有趣，因为我小时候上初中时，有一个朋友。

sentences.en: And she and I became obsessed with this Ouija board that I had.
sentences.zh: 我和她对我拥有的那个通灵板着了迷。

sentences.en: And we would use it together.
sentences.zh: 我们会一起使用它。

sentences.en: And it would spell out all kinds of words.
sentences.zh: 它会拼出各种各样的词。

sentences.en: And it would send us on expeditions around the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 它还会带我们去社区周围探险。

sentences.en: And it had just a whole series of personalities and rituals that we were supposed to go through.
sentences.zh: 它有一整套我们必须经历的个性和仪式。

sentences.en: Now, I was not pushing that little table.
sentences.zh: 当时，我并没有推那个小板子。

sentences.en: And I still know where this woman is.
sentences.zh: 而且我至今还知道这个人在哪里。

sentences.en: And she swears to this day that she wasn't pushing the little table.
sentences.zh: 她至今发誓说她没有推那个小板子。

sentences.en: So how does your work explain what may have been going on?
sentences.zh: 那么你的工作是如何解释当时可能发生的事情的呢？

sentences.en: Were we not in touch with – they called it Ouija control.
sentences.zh: 我们是不是没有联系上——他们称之为通灵控制。

sentences.en: I mean, the board would tell me that there was a place called Ouija control.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，板子会告诉我有一个叫通灵控制的地方。

sentences.en: That's a new one on me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是个新鲜事。

sentences.en: I like that idea.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个想法。

sentences.en: Now, I think we could be pretty sure that, in fact, between you, you were pushing the little clime shed.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为我们可以相当肯定，实际上，你们两个当时都在推那个小板子。

sentences.en: But you weren't consciously aware of it.
sentences.zh: 但你们并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: And I totally know where you're coming from.
sentences.zh: 我完全理解你的意思。

sentences.en: Because as an undergraduate student, in my final year at Manchester University, I would go out on the Friday night and go to the pub and have a few drinks.
sentences.zh: 因为作为曼彻斯特大学最后一年的本科生，我会在周五晚上出去，去酒吧喝几杯。

sentences.en: I lived in a house with five other guys.
sentences.zh: 我和另外五个家伙住在一栋房子里。

sentences.en: And it was a regular thing that we'd do when we got back in just to entertain ourselves, would play around with the Ouija board.
sentences.zh: 我们回来后经常做的一件事就是玩通灵板来娱乐自己。

sentences.en: And it does feel very much like, I'm not pushing this.
sentences.zh: 它确实感觉非常像，我没有推它。

sentences.en: I'm not pushing this.
sentences.zh: 我没有推它。

sentences.en: It's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Again, one of the kind of nicest illustrations of the fact that this is what we call the idiomotory effect, where basically non-conscious muscular movements, that, again,
sentences.zh: 同样，这说明了我们所说的意动效应，即基本上是非意识的肌肉运动，这再次，

sentences.en: if we look back in the history of this, at the time of the heyday of seances back in the Victorian era,
sentences.zh: 如果我们回顾这段历史，在维多利亚时代降神会盛行的时候，

sentences.en: another craze that caught on initially from America and then came over to Europe was what's called table turning or table tilting.
sentences.zh: 另一种最初从美国流行起来并传到欧洲的热潮被称为桌子转动或桌子倾斜。

sentences.en: And this was, again, supposed to be a way of contacting the spirits where you take a small wooden table.
sentences.zh: 这再次被认为是联系灵魂的一种方式，你拿一张小木桌。

sentences.en: The sitters would put their hands on the tabletop and they'd ask questions.
sentences.zh: 参与者把手放在桌面上，然后提问。

sentences.en: And the table, on a good session, the table would kind of shudder in response to the questions.
sentences.zh: 在一次好的降神会上，桌子会随着问题而颤抖。

sentences.en: On a very good session, it could even end up, it appeared that people were trying to chase the table around the room, trying to keep their hands in contact with it.
sentences.zh: 在一次非常好的降神会上，甚至看起来人们在追着桌子满屋子跑，试图让他们的手保持与桌子的接触。

sentences.en: All very, very exciting stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都非常非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And this caught the attention of Sir Michael Faraday.
sentences.zh: 这引起了迈克尔·法拉第爵士的注意。

sentences.en: And what I really like about this is that rather than just dismissing it, he thought, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我真正喜欢的是，他没有直接否定它，而是想，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Let's have a look at it.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看。

sentences.en: So there are two possibilities here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有两种可能性。

sentences.en: One is that some external force, possibly a spirit, is moving the table, or in the case of the Ouija board, the planchette or the wine glass.
sentences.zh: 一种是某种外部力量，可能是灵魂，在移动桌子，或者在通灵板的情况下，是移动指示器或酒杯。

sentences.en: Or people are pushing the table without realising it.
sentences.zh: 或者人们在不知不觉中推着桌子。

sentences.en: And Faraday devised a number of ingenious experiments.
sentences.zh: 法拉第设计了许多巧妙的实验。

sentences.en: I'll just mention one of them.
sentences.zh: 我只提其中一个。

sentences.en: Instead of having people put their hands directly on the tabletop, he had layers of waxed paper on the tabletop.
sentences.zh: 他没有让人们直接把手放在桌面上，而是在桌面上放了几层蜡纸。

sentences.en: And they put their hands on top of the layers of waxed paper.
sentences.zh: 他们把手放在蜡纸层上。

sentences.en: Now, if you think about it, if the table moves to the right, if the table's moved on its own, the waxed papers, the hands will tend to drag behind a little bit.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你仔细想想，如果桌子向右移动，如果桌子是自己移动的，蜡纸和手会倾向于稍微滞后。

sentences.en: And the waxed papers would spread out to the left.
sentences.zh: 蜡纸会向左散开。

sentences.en: If the hands are pushing the table, then the table will drag behind the hands a little bit.
sentences.zh: 如果手在推桌子，那么桌子会稍微滞后于手。

sentences.en: And the waxed papers, the wax sheets would be pushed to the right.
sentences.zh: 蜡纸和蜡片会被推向右边。

sentences.en: Well, you can guess what he actually found.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以猜到他实际上发现了什么。

sentences.en: So even those people, these people were convinced they were not pushing the table around.
sentences.zh: 所以即使这些人确信他们没有推桌子。

sentences.en: Actually, they were.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们确实推了。

sentences.en: And again, we know from a number of different studies that that is almost certainly what's going on in these situations.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们从许多不同的研究中知道，在这些情况下，几乎可以肯定这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: What role does inattentional blindness play in having us kind of feel that there are supernatural things occurring around us?
sentences.zh: 非注意盲视在让我们感觉到周围发生超自然事物方面起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: I think it's just one example of a situation where, because we're not aware of the limitations of our cognitive system,
sentences.zh: 我认为这只是一个例子，因为我们没有意识到我们认知系统的局限性，

sentences.en: we make various assumptions about how much information we take in, how accurate our memory is, etc., etc.
sentences.zh: 我们对我们接收了多少信息、我们的记忆有多准确等等做了各种假设。

sentences.en: So inattentional blindness refers to a situation where there might be a stimulus that you're actually looking directly at, but you don't see it.
sentences.zh: 所以非注意盲视是指这样一种情况：可能有一个你实际上正直接看着的刺激物，但你没有看到它。

sentences.en: You don't perceive it.
sentences.zh: 你没有感知到它。

sentences.en: And the classic example of this is the famous invisible gorilla study, of course.
sentences.zh: 这方面的经典例子当然是著名的隐形大猩猩研究。

sentences.en: Me and my wife, who's also a psychologist, we kind of looked at this because she was doing lots of research into the topic of inattentional blindness.
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子，她也是一名心理学家，我们研究过这个问题，因为她当时正在对非注意盲视这一课题进行大量研究。

sentences.en: She contacted me one day to say, do you have a copy of a scale that we could use to measure absorption?
sentences.zh: 有一天她联系我，问我是否有可以用来测量专注度的量表副本？

sentences.en: Absorption is the tendency that people have to become completely engrossed in what they're doing and to completely cut off the kind of outside world.
sentences.zh: 专注度是指人们完全沉浸在他们正在做的事情中，并完全切断外部世界的那种倾向。

sentences.en: So you have the kind of people who, when they read a book or watch a film, just get completely engrossed in it, and hence absorption.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有那种人，当他们读书或看电影时，会完全沉浸其中，因此产生了专注度。

sentences.en: I did have such a scale.
sentences.zh: 我确实有这样一个量表。

sentences.en: And my wife was basically interested in the issue of, well, you'd expect people who scored highly on this measure to be maybe more susceptible to inattentional blindness.
sentences.zh: 我妻子主要对这个问题感兴趣，就是说，你可能会认为在这个量表上得分高的人，可能更容易受到非注意盲视的影响。

sentences.en: They might not note, if they're in the gorilla study, for example, they might be the ones that,
sentences.zh: 他们可能不会注意到，比如如果他们参与了大猩猩实验，他们可能就是那些……

sentences.en: because they were concentrating on the primary task to count the number of times the ball was thrown, they wouldn't see the gorilla.
sentences.zh: 因为他们专注于数球被投掷次数的主要任务，所以他们看不到大猩猩。

sentences.en: Which sounded sensible.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很有道理。

sentences.en: Now, I knew that absorption correlates with paranormal belief and experience.
sentences.zh: 当时我知道“沉浸感”与超自然信仰和经历有关。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, let's see it'd be interesting to look at all of this in one study.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，如果能在同一项研究中观察所有这些因素，那会很有趣。

sentences.en: So that's what we did.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: We didn't use the gorilla task.
sentences.zh: 我们没有使用大猩猩任务。

sentences.en: We used something that was conceptually similar.
sentences.zh: 我们使用了一个概念上类似的任务。

sentences.en: My wife programmed the computers so that you saw a display of white letters and black letters moving around the screen.
sentences.zh: 我妻子编写了程序，让屏幕上显示白色和黑色的字母在四处移动。

sentences.en: The letters would kind of bounce off the edge of the screen as they moved around.
sentences.zh: 这些字母在移动时会从屏幕边缘反弹。

sentences.en: And halfway through, a big red cross moved slowly across the background.
sentences.zh: 在进行到一半时，一个巨大的红色十字架缓慢地穿过背景。

sentences.en: That was our gorilla.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们的“大猩猩”。

sentences.en: And the task was set up so that about half the people at the end of the task, if you said, did you notice anything unusual or even more directly, did you see a red cross?
sentences.zh: 任务设置是这样的：在任务结束时，如果你问大约一半的人“你注意到什么异常了吗？”或者更直接地问“你看到一个红色的十字架了吗？”，

sentences.en: About half the people would report they had seen it and half hadn't.
sentences.zh: 大约有一半人会说他们看到了，另一半人则没有。

sentences.en: What we found, as we predicted, was that the people who scored, the ones who didn't see the red cross,
sentences.zh: 正如我们所预测的那样，我们发现那些得分较高的人，也就是那些没看到红色十字架的人，

sentences.en: the inattentionally blind participants, scored higher overall on the absorption scale, also scored higher on paranormal belief and experience.
sentences.zh: 那些出现非注意盲视的参与者，在沉浸感量表上的总分更高，在超自然信仰和经历上的得分也更高。

sentences.en: And, you know, we replicated this effect in a second study.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们在第二项研究中重复了这个实验，效果依然存在。

sentences.en: So it does seem to be a real effect.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是一个真实存在的效应。

sentences.en: Now, kind of bringing that back to kind of more real life situations where people might think they've encountered a ghoSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，把这个结论带回到现实生活中，人们可能会认为自己遇到了鬼魂。

sentences.en: And again, it's maybe worth pointing out here that when people talk about ghostly encounters,
sentences.zh: 再次指出这一点可能很有意义，当人们谈论鬼魂遭遇时，

sentences.en: I think that summons up an image of a translucent figure floating and coming through the wall and so on.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会让人联想到一个半透明的人影漂浮着穿过墙壁之类的画面。

sentences.en: But typically it's not that.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况并非如此。

sentences.en: It's more likely to be that people report that objects have been moved and they didn't know how they were moved.
sentences.zh: 更有可能的情况是，人们报告说物体被移动了，而他们不知道是怎么移动的。

sentences.en: Or maybe, like we were talking about before, a sense of presence.
sentences.zh: 或者就像我们之前讨论的那样，有一种“被注视感”。

sentences.en: It's much more kind of subtle effects rather than a full apparition experience.
sentences.zh: 这更多是一种微妙的效应，而不是完整的显灵体验。

sentences.en: So someone who, for example, insists that they've had a paranormal experience because this is just a hypothetical example.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，有人坚持说他们有过超自然体验，因为这只是一个假设的例子，

sentences.en: You know, they were in a room and an object moved from one place to another and there was nobody else in the room.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们在一个房间里，一个物体从一个地方移动到了另一个地方，而房间里没有其他人。

sentences.en: Then, well, yeah, maybe you, you know, somebody else was in the room and they moved the object.
sentences.zh: 那么，好吧，也许，你知道，房间里有别人，是他们移动了物体。

sentences.en: You just didn't see them.
sentences.zh: 你只是没看见他们。

sentences.en: Oh, but I'm sure I would have done.
sentences.zh: “哦，但我确信我一定会看到的。”

sentences.en: I would have done.
sentences.zh: “我一定会看到的。”

sentences.en: You know, well, would you?
sentences.zh: 你知道，真的会吗？

sentences.en: People don't see a gorilla.
sentences.zh: 人们连大猩猩都看不到。

sentences.en: And there have been so many variations on that basic study that we know that people don't often see things that they are sure they would see.
sentences.zh: 那个基础研究已经有了很多变体，我们知道人们往往看不到那些他们确信自己一定会看到的东西。

sentences.en: So, again, just providing a mundane explanation for an ostensibly mysterious event.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次强调，这只是为看似神秘的事件提供了一个世俗的解释。

sentences.en: And for those few listeners who don't know the Invisible Gorilla study, can you just summarize that?
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道“隐形大猩猩”研究的听众，你能简单总结一下吗？

sentences.en: Yes, certainly.
sentences.zh: 好的，当然可以。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This was a classic study in 1999 by Simons and Shabris.
sentences.zh: 这是西蒙斯和沙布里斯在1999年进行的一项经典研究。

sentences.en: What they did was to show people a short video clip of two groups of people standing there, some in white shirts, some in black shirts.
sentences.zh: 他们向人们展示了一段简短的视频片段，视频中有两组人站在那里，一些穿白衬衫，一些穿黑衬衫。

sentences.en: And each group were throwing a ball back in two to each other.
sentences.zh: 每组人都在互相传球。

sentences.en: And the task was to count the number of times that the people in the white shirts threw the ball to each other, ignore the people in the black shirts.
sentences.zh: 任务是数出穿白衬衫的人互相传球的次数，忽略穿黑衬衫的人。

sentences.en: And halfway through the video, somebody walks into the middle of the group in a gorilla suit, stands there beating their chest and then walks off.
sentences.zh: 视频进行到一半时，一个穿着大猩猩服装的人走进人群中间，站在那里捶胸顿足，然后走开。

sentences.en: Now, you think intuitively this is something that would be bound to capture your attention, even though it's not what you've been asked to do, that you would notice it.
sentences.zh: 你直觉上会认为这一定会吸引你的注意力，即使这不是让你做的事，你也一定会注意到它。

sentences.en: About half the people who do that test don't see the gorilla.
sentences.zh: 但大约有一半做这个测试的人没看到大猩猩。

sentences.en: And it's a lovely example.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, again, they were shocked by the results themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们自己也被结果震惊了。

sentences.en: They didn't expect that to get such a strong effect, but it's something that has been replicated to the nth degree.
sentences.zh: 他们没想到会有这么强烈的效应，但这已经被无数次重复验证过了。

sentences.en: It's definitely real.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是真实的。

sentences.en: And it's got real implications, obviously, in real life.
sentences.zh: 显然，它在现实生活中也有实际意义。

sentences.en: There's a lot of fatal accidents, of course, by people not seeing something that was right there.
sentences.zh: 当然，有很多致命事故是因为人们没看到就在眼前的东西。

sentences.en: They were pointing their eyes at it.
sentences.zh: 他们的眼睛盯着它看。

sentences.en: They just didn't register it.
sentences.zh: 但大脑就是没有登记到它。

sentences.en: So it's generated a lot of further research.
sentences.zh: 所以它引发了大量的后续研究。

sentences.en: We cover a broad range of psychology topics in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在本播客中涵盖了广泛的心理学主题。

sentences.en: And I'm struck by the common themes that have come up in recent episodes.
sentences.zh: 最近几期节目中出现的一些共同主题让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: We've done episodes on conspiracy theories, superstition, science denial, memory errors,
sentences.zh: 我们做过关于阴谋论、迷信、科学否定主义、记忆错误的节目，

sentences.en: and many similar issues that seem to emerge in terms of how our biases and other cognitive glitches can lead us astray.
sentences.zh: 以及许多类似的问题，这些问题似乎都反映了我们的偏见和其他认知缺陷是如何将我们引入歧途的。

sentences.en: So do you see a connection between anomalistic psychology and research on these other topics like science denial and conspiracies?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为异常心理学与科学否定主义和阴谋论等其他主题的研究之间有什么联系吗？

sentences.en: Oh, very much so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常有联系。

sentences.en: I mean, conspiracy theories, I'd say in recent years, our research in terms of the areas that we've been actively researching, there have been three main ones.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于阴谋论，我想说近年来，在我们积极研究的领域中，主要有三个方向。

sentences.en: One has been sleep paralysis, one has been false memories, and the third has been belief in conspiracies.
sentences.zh: 一个是睡眠瘫痪，一个是虚假记忆，第三个是阴谋论信仰。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of, you know, they all kind of are linked to each other quite strongly.
sentences.zh: 它们之间有着非常紧密的联系。

sentences.en: It's really, I mean, I'm fascinated by the whole topic of weird beliefs and where do they come from?
sentences.zh: 我真的对“奇怪的信仰”这个话题很着迷，它们到底从何而来？

sentences.en: There are many conspiracy theories that do have an explicitly paranormal angle to them.
sentences.zh: 许多阴谋论确实带有明确的超自然色彩。

sentences.en: Obviously, they don't all have.
sentences.zh: 当然，并非所有阴谋论都如此。

sentences.en: But so many kind of links between the kind of factors which influence whether or not people believe in conspiracies, whether or not people believe in the paranormal,
sentences.zh: 但在影响人们是否相信阴谋论、是否相信超自然现象、

sentences.en: the supernatural, alternative medicine.
sentences.zh: 灵异现象、替代医学的因素之间，存在着太多的联系。

sentences.en: The list goes on.
sentences.zh: 名单还在继续。

sentences.en: I'm an atheist, so I would even put religious beliefs into that category.
sentences.zh: 我是一个无神论者，所以我甚至会把宗教信仰也归入这一类。

sentences.en: These are all what I would classify as examples of magical thinking.
sentences.zh: 我将这些统称为“魔法思维”的例子。

sentences.en: And interestingly, they all tend to increase, our tendencies towards magical thinking tend to increase at times of stress and uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它们往往都会增加，我们在压力和不确定时期，对魔法思维的倾向往往会增加。

sentences.en: And that seems to go across the board for all of them.
sentences.zh: 这似乎适用于所有这些情况。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of other parallels as well, which is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但还有许多其他的相似之处，这非常迷人。

sentences.en: Now, you've done research to directly test whether paranormal claims might be for real.
sentences.zh: 你做过直接测试超自然主张是否真实的研究。

sentences.en: Can you talk about some of these studies?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈其中一些研究吗？

sentences.en: So how do you test, for example, whether ESP exists?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何测试超感知觉（ESP）是否存在呢？

sentences.en: With respect to testing ESP, there are a number of established ways of doing it.
sentences.zh: 关于测试ESP，已经有了一些既定的方法。

sentences.en: One technique which I've never actually used personally, but one which is still something of a challenge for skeptics to explain away.
sentences.zh: 有一种技术我个人从未用过，但它仍然是怀疑论者难以解释的挑战。

sentences.en: I'm not convinced overall, otherwise I wouldn't be a skeptic.
sentences.zh: 我总体上并不信服，否则我就不会是怀疑论者了。

sentences.en: But the so-called Gansfeld technique, this is based on the idea that if there is such a thing as ESP, then it's maybe a very weak signal,
sentences.zh: 但所谓的“甘兹菲尔德实验”（Gansfeld technique），其基础理念是：如果真的存在ESP，那么它可能是一个非常微弱的信号，

sentences.en: which is usually kind of drowned out by all the other processing that's going on in our brains at the time.
sentences.zh: 通常会被我们大脑当时正在进行的所有其他处理过程所淹没。

sentences.en: Now, if there's anything in that idea, the things to do would be to try and dampen down the background activity so that the ESP signal, the telepathy signal can come through.
sentences.zh: 如果这个想法有道理，那么要做的事情就是设法抑制背景活动，以便ESP信号、心灵感应信号能够显现出来。

sentences.en: So what people do is you get a sender and a receiver, two people taking part in the study.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的做法是找一个发送者和一个接收者，两个人参与研究。

sentences.en: The sender relaxes on a comfortable couch, wears headphones over which you play white noise.
sentences.zh: 发送者躺在舒适的沙发上放松，戴着耳机，耳机里播放着白噪音。

sentences.en: They have half ping pong balls over their eyes with cotton wool around them and maybe a red light bulb.
sentences.zh: 他们的眼睛上盖着乒乓球的一半，周围塞着棉花，可能还有一个红灯泡。

sentences.en: So if they open their eyes, all they see is red.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们睁开眼睛，看到的只有红色。

sentences.en: Basically, you're trying to kind of, it's like perceptual deprivation.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你是在尝试进行一种感知剥夺。

sentences.en: And it's a very comfortable position to be in.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常舒适的姿势。

sentences.en: And people typically report that when they're in that situation, they enter a very relaxed state and their mind fills with imagery,
sentences.zh: 人们通常报告说，在这种情况下，他们会进入一种非常放松的状态，大脑中充满了意象，

sentences.en: which is quite a common thing if you're just lying there on your own couch.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是独自躺在沙发上，这很常见。

sentences.en: And the hope is that this is a kind of state that would be conducive to being able to receive these weak ESP signals.
sentences.zh: 希望这种状态有助于接收这些微弱的ESP信号。

sentences.en: So at prearranged times, you have somebody in a distant location who randomly selects, it used to be kind of pictures that people would look at, often kind of art, postcards,
sentences.zh: 所以在预定的时间，在遥远的地方有人随机选择一些图片，过去通常是人们观看的图片，通常是艺术品、明信片之类的东西。

sentences.en: that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 之类的东西。

sentences.en: These days, it tends to be video clips.
sentences.zh: 现在，通常是视频片段。

sentences.en: You randomly select a set of typically four, let's say, video clips, and then randomly select one clip from within those.
sentences.zh: 你随机选择一组（通常是四个）视频片段，然后从中随机选择一个。

sentences.en: And that person, the sender, watches the video and tries to telepathically transmit the information back to the receiver.
sentences.zh: 那个人，即发送者，观看视频并试图通过心灵感应将信息传回给接收者。

sentences.en: There are variations on a theme, but essentially what would often happen is that the experimenter who is with the receiver would note down, they'd record everything that's said.
sentences.zh: 虽然有各种变体，但本质上通常发生的情况是，与接收者在一起的实验者会记下并记录下所说的一切。

sentences.en: Instead, the experimenter who must not know what the target is themselves in case they give away any unconscious cues, maybe at the end of the session, they'd go over it and say,
sentences.zh: 实验者本人绝不能知道目标是什么，以免泄露任何潜意识线索，也许在会议结束时，他们会回顾并说，

sentences.en: you know, you said something about triangular shapes.
sentences.zh: “你提到了一些三角形的形状。”

sentences.en: Could you just describe that a little bit more clearly just to get it all clarified and all recorded?
sentences.zh: “你能描述得更清楚一点吗？以便把一切都澄清并记录下来。”

sentences.en: But the clincher is when either the receiver or independent judges say what is the best match from the four available video clips to the imagery that the person was describing.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，当接收者或独立评判员说出四个可用视频片段中与该人描述的意象最匹配的是哪一个时。

sentences.en: Now, you would expect by chance people to get a hit rate of 25%, but it was claimed that people were getting hit rates of more like 33%.
sentences.zh: 按理说，人们的命中率应该是25%，但据称人们的命中率达到了33%左右。

sentences.en: So not a massive effect, but statistically significant.
sentences.zh: 所以效应虽然不大，但在统计学上是显著的。

sentences.en: That's one example.
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子。

sentences.en: Now, there are issues, which, again, we would probably need another three podcasts to talk about, which mean that, yeah,
sentences.zh: 当然，还有一些问题，我们可能需要再做三个播客才能谈完，这意味着，是的，

sentences.en: although I think the evidence there is quite interesting and worth taking seriously, which a lot of sceptics don't, and I think they should.
sentences.zh: 虽然我认为那里的证据相当有趣，值得认真对待，而许多怀疑论者并不这么认为，但我认为他们应该这样做。

sentences.en: I think they're kind of missing a trick there.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们错过了一些关键点。

sentences.en: There are studies like that.
sentences.zh: 确实有这样的研究。

sentences.en: There are techniques like that where you can statistically analyse the results, where you can try your best to be as methodologically sound as you can.
sentences.zh: 有这样的技术，你可以对结果进行统计分析，你可以尽最大努力在方法论上做到尽可能严谨。

sentences.en: And not all of those results can be just dismissed by the sceptics.
sentences.zh: 并非所有这些结果都能被怀疑论者轻易驳回。

sentences.en: And that leads me to the idea of how your thinking has evolved over time, right?
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了你的思维是如何随时间演变的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you were a believer in parapsychology when you were quite young, and then you changed your thinking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你年轻时曾是超心理学的信徒，后来你改变了想法。

sentences.en: At one point, you thought parapsychology was a pseudoscience, but now you don't think that.
sentences.zh: 曾经有一段时间，你认为超心理学是伪科学，但现在你不这么认为了。

sentences.en: What went through your...
sentences.zh: 是什么让你……

sentences.en: I mean, how did you reach this point?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是如何走到这一步的？

sentences.en: For me, kind of discovering the joys of scepticism, it was a very exciting time in my life, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，发现怀疑论的乐趣是我生命中非常激动人心的时刻，我必须得说。

sentences.en: I'd always had an interest in these kind of things.
sentences.zh: 我一直对这类事情很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Not an overwhelming passion, but I'd always had an interest in kind of ghost stories and UFOs and just weird stuff generally, you know, like a lot of teenagers.
sentences.zh: 不是那种压倒性的热情，但我一直对鬼故事、UFO和各种奇怪的事情感兴趣，你知道，就像很多青少年一样。

sentences.en: And pretty much everything I'd read was very uncritical.
sentences.zh: 而且我读过的几乎所有东西都非常缺乏批判性。

sentences.en: It was very kind of pro-paranormal.
sentences.zh: 它们非常倾向于支持超自然现象。

sentences.en: And so why should I question it, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以我为什么要质疑它呢，对吧？

sentences.en: It was only when I was doing my PhD at Leicester University in a completely different area, nothing to do with anomalistic psychology,
sentences.zh: 直到我在莱斯特大学攻读博士学位时，研究的是一个完全不同的领域，与异常心理学无关，

sentences.en: someone recommended a book to me.
sentences.zh: 有人向我推荐了一本书。

sentences.en: It was by James Alcock.
sentences.zh: 作者是詹姆斯·奥尔科克（James Alcock）。

sentences.en: It was called Parapsychology, Science or Magic.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《超心理学：科学还是魔法》。

sentences.en: And that book kind of basically changed my life.
sentences.zh: 那本书基本上改变了我的生活。

sentences.en: You know, it opened up the doors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它为我打开了大门。

sentences.en: It was written by a social psychologist who was very informed on parapsychology, but was a sceptic.
sentences.zh: 它是由一位对超心理学非常了解但持怀疑态度的社会心理学家写的。

sentences.en: And he was presenting basically non-paranormal accounts for a range of ostensibly paranormal experiences.
sentences.zh: 他基本上为一系列看似超自然的体验提供了非超自然的解释。

sentences.en: And I found it all very, very kind of convincing and really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我发现这一切都非常非常有说服力，而且真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And that's when I first kind of became a sceptic, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 那就是我第一次成为所谓的“怀疑论者”的时候。

sentences.en: And I obviously then kind of realised that there were sceptical books out there.
sentences.zh: 显然，我后来意识到市面上还有很多怀疑论书籍。

sentences.en: There were people like James Randi and Ray Hyman and all these other great people doing really interesting stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有像詹姆斯·兰迪（James Randi）和雷·海曼（Ray Hyman）这样伟大的学者在做非常有趣的研究。

sentences.en: I shouldn't blame them for one aspect of this was that I initially had the impression that parapsychology was a pseudoscience,
sentences.zh: 我不应该责怪他们，但我最初的印象是超心理学是伪科学，

sentences.en: kind of no better than astrology in that respect, and various other kind of attitudes that all parapsychologists were kind of incompetent.
sentences.zh: 在这方面不比占星术好多少，而且还有各种态度，认为所有的超心理学家都是无能的。

sentences.en: They didn't know how to design experiments or analyse data or any of these things.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道如何设计实验、分析数据或做任何这些事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, various other kind of attitudes, which I would now kind of say were, you know, too negative, too extreme.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，还有其他各种态度，我现在会说这些态度太负面、太极端了。

sentences.en: And it was only kind of over the years as I then gradually got to actually meet a number of real life parapsychologists.
sentences.zh: 直到多年后，我逐渐有机会真正见到一些现实生活中的超心理学家。

sentences.en: I realised that this wasn't actually true.
sentences.zh: 我意识到这其实并不是真的。

sentences.en: Again, one person that I would kind of particularly know here would be the late Professor Robert Morris,
sentences.zh: 再次强调，我在这里特别想提到的一位是已故的罗伯特·莫里斯（Robert Morris）教授，

sentences.en: Bob Morris up at Edinburgh, the Kerstler Chair in Parapsychology.
sentences.zh: 爱丁堡大学的鲍勃·莫里斯，凯斯特勒超心理学讲座教授。

sentences.en: And his protégé, who is now the current Kerstler Chair, Caroline Watt, who's a very good friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 还有他的门生，也就是现在的凯斯特勒讲座教授卡罗琳·瓦特（Caroline Watt），她是我非常好的朋友。

sentences.en: Two people who were probably, certainly Bob and maybe less so Caroline,
sentences.zh: 这两个人，当然鲍勃肯定是，卡罗琳可能稍微少一点，

sentences.en: but Bob was definitely more of a believer than a sceptic, but he was very open to listen to what sceptics had to say.
sentences.zh: 但鲍勃绝对是一个信徒多于怀疑论者，但他非常愿意倾听怀疑论者的意见。

sentences.en: I really like that kind of open-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢那种开放的心态。

sentences.en: And also he had kind of, there were two strands to the work.
sentences.zh: 而且他也有，他的工作有两个方向。

sentences.en: There was looking to see whether maybe things like telepathy, precognition, et cetera, et cetera, really did exiSt.
sentences.zh: 一个是观察像心灵感应、预知等现象是否真的存在。

sentences.en: That was one strand.
sentences.zh: 那只是其中一个方面。

sentences.en: And that's probably what the major emphasis of that unit was about.
sentences.zh: 那可能也是该单元重点强调的内容。

sentences.en: But also a second strand, looking at why people might sometimes think they've had a paranormal experience when in fact they hadn't.
sentences.zh: 但还有第二个方面，即研究为什么人们有时会认为自己有了超自然体验，而实际上并没有。

sentences.en: I mean, Bob's first PhD student was my good friend, Richard Wiseman, who is one of the kind of leading sceptics in terms of all this stuff as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，鲍勃的第一位博士生是我的一位好朋友，理查德·怀斯曼，他也是这类议题中主要的怀疑论者之一。

sentences.en: And so, as I say, for many years in my lectures, I would talk about pseudoscience generally.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我所说，多年来在我的讲座中，我都会谈论伪科学。

sentences.en: But when I talked about parapsychology, it was as pseudoscience, as I then saw it.
sentences.zh: 但当我谈到超心理学时，我当时将其视为伪科学。

sentences.en: And then I came across a paper where somebody had put this to the test empirically by looking at the typical kind of criticisms in terms of the criteria for pseudoscience that sceptics direct to parapsychology.
sentences.zh: 后来我偶然读到一篇论文，有人通过实证检验，审视了怀疑论者针对超心理学所提出的关于伪科学标准的典型批评。

sentences.en: And it's basically said, well, you know, are they true?
sentences.zh: 基本上就是问，这些批评是真的吗？

sentences.en: By looking at three journals from kind of mainstream science, including the British Journal of Psychology, three journals from fringe sciences,
sentences.zh: 通过观察三本主流科学期刊（包括《英国心理学杂志》）和三本边缘科学期刊，

sentences.en: including the Journal of Parapsychology.
sentences.zh: 包括《超心理学杂志》。

sentences.en: And really, on that basis, it didn't look like these were fair criticisms, the vast majority of them.
sentences.zh: 实际上，基于此，这些批评中的绝大多数似乎并不公正。

sentences.en: And so, on that basis, and ultimately, science is a method rather than a body of established facts.
sentences.zh: 因此，基于这一点，归根结底，科学是一种方法，而不是一套既定的事实。

sentences.en: And you can look at any issue, either scientifically or non-scientifically.
sentences.zh: 你可以用科学或非科学的方式看待任何问题。

sentences.en: But if you're looking at an issue scientifically, using methodological controls and statistical analysis and so on and so forth, why would you not say that's a science?
sentences.zh: 但如果你用科学的方法，即使用方法论控制、统计分析等等来审视一个问题，为什么不称其为科学呢？

sentences.en: And so, again, one final argument, people like myself, Richard Wiseman, James Randi, a whole host of other sceptics have sometimes directly tested paranormal claims,
sentences.zh: 所以，再重申一个最终论点，像我、理查德·怀斯曼、詹姆斯·兰迪以及其他许多怀疑论者，有时会直接测试超自然主张，

sentences.en: in which case we're doing parapsychology, and I would hope we're doing it scientifically.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们就是在做超心理学研究，而且我希望我们是以科学的方式在做。

sentences.en: So parapsychology, at its best, I think has to be described as a science.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，超心理学在最好的情况下，必须被描述为一门科学。

sentences.en: This is not a popular view among sceptics, I hasten to add.
sentences.zh: 我得补充一句，这在怀疑论者中并不是一个普遍的观点。

sentences.en: Our sceptics would disagree, but that's my position now.
sentences.zh: 我们的怀疑论者会不同意，但这就是我现在的立场。

sentences.en: But essentially, I mean, if you design a study scientifically, you know, you could potentially study anything, I mean, as long as you're following the prescribed method.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，如果你以科学的方式设计研究，只要你遵循规定的方法，理论上你可以研究任何东西。

sentences.en: But, you know, that raises another question in my mind, which is that there have been studies that have been published in esteemed journals, peer-reviewed journals,
sentences.zh: 但是，这在我脑海中引发了另一个问题，那就是有一些研究发表在受人尊敬的同行评审期刊上，

sentences.en: about parapsychology, and some of them have indicated an existence, and then some of them have been retracted.
sentences.zh: 关于超心理学的，其中一些指出了其存在，但后来又被撤稿了。

sentences.en: So, you know, why is that happening?
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么会发生这种情况？

sentences.en: Is that because we're not sceptical enough?
sentences.zh: 是因为我们不够怀疑吗？

sentences.en: I think it's, I mean, it is one of those, obviously, hugely controversial areas, and people, you know, emotions are high on both sides.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这显然是那些极具争议的领域之一，双方的情绪都很激动。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the most recent episodes would be kind of Daryl Bem's controversial paper on precognition.
sentences.zh: 最近的一个例子是达里尔·贝姆关于预知的争议性论文。

sentences.en: And that was published in, I think it was 2011.
sentences.zh: 那发表于2011年，我想是这样。

sentences.en: Again, without going into all the details, Bem, who has obviously been around for many, many decades, very respected figure within psychology, but also,
sentences.zh: 同样，无需赘述细节，贝姆显然已经活跃了几十年，是心理学界非常受人尊敬的人物，但同时，

sentences.en: unusually for a psychologist, known to be very sympathetic towards parapsychology and paranormal claiMs.
sentences.zh: 作为心理学家，他不同寻常地对超心理学和超自然主张表现出非常同情的态度。

sentences.en: And he had already done this before, with respect to the Gansfeld studies, rather than publishing in parapsychology journals,
sentences.zh: 他之前在“甘兹菲尔德实验”方面也做过类似的事情，而不是在超心理学期刊上发表，

sentences.en: where the kind of mainstream science media wouldn't even bother to read the stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为主流科学媒体甚至懒得去读那些东西。

sentences.en: He'd made a point of trying to publish in really the top journals in psychology and succeeded on at least two occasions.
sentences.zh: 他特意尝试在顶尖心理学期刊上发表文章，并且至少成功了两次。

sentences.en: And it's kind of interesting when somebody does that, because it raises all kinds of issues.
sentences.zh: 当有人这样做时，这很有趣，因为它引发了各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: Just to kind of summarise, he published in the more recent study, the studies of precognition, there were nine experiments, over a thousand participants in total.
sentences.zh: 简单总结一下，他在最近的研究中发表了关于预知的研究，共有九个实验，总共一千多名参与者。

sentences.en: And basically, he was arguing that he had found kind of pretty compelling evidence for the reality of people being able to sense future events before they happen, precognition.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他认为自己找到了相当令人信服的证据，证明人们能够感知未来事件，即预知。

sentences.en: One of the very good things that he did, this paper, I hasten to add, had been through, I think it was half a dozen different referees, the standard refereeing process.
sentences.zh: 他做的一件非常好的事情是，我得补充一下，这篇论文经过了我想大概六位不同的审稿人，即标准的同行评审过程。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, the editor had felt that he had no choice other than to publish, even though he probably knew that he was going to be a very controversial paper.
sentences.zh: 最终，编辑觉得除了发表别无选择，尽管他可能知道这会是一篇非常有争议的论文。

sentences.en: One of the good things about what Ben did was to say he wanted other people to try and replicate the effects and he would make his software available.
sentences.zh: 贝姆所做的好事之一是，他表示希望其他人尝试复现这些效应，并且他会提供他的软件。

sentences.en: We decided to chase up on that, we being, in this case, Richard Wiseman and Stuart Ritchie.
sentences.zh: 我们决定跟进，我们指的是理查德·怀斯曼和我，斯图尔特·里奇。

sentences.en: I must admit, we had a slightly ulterior motive here.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我们在这里有一个稍微不可告人的动机。

sentences.en: We didn't really expect to replicate the effects, but we did think this might be a relatively easy way to get a paper in a top journal.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真的期望能复现这些效应，但我们确实认为这可能是一种相对容易在顶尖期刊上发表论文的方法。

sentences.en: That was our hope.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的希望。

sentences.en: But anyway, it still took a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，这仍然需要大量的工作。

sentences.en: We each did an independent replication of BEM's experiment number nine.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都对贝姆的第九个实验进行了独立的复现。

sentences.en: I can go into the details of what the experiment involved with you like, but just for the time being, I'll talk about the fact we didn't get the same results as BEM.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，我可以详细介绍实验涉及的内容，但目前我只想说，我们没有得到和贝姆一样的结果。

sentences.en: We weren't surprised.
sentences.zh: 我们并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: We wrote it up.
sentences.zh: 我们把它写了下来。

sentences.en: We sent it into the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, and it was rejected without being sent out for peer review.
sentences.zh: 我们把它投给了《人格与社会心理学杂志》，结果在没有送交同行评审的情况下就被拒稿了。

sentences.en: And that's what really annoyed us, because BEM's paper had had huge coverage right around the world.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我们很恼火，因为贝姆的论文在全世界范围内得到了巨大的报道。

sentences.en: So it's important whether these effects are real or not, and we had failed to replicate.
sentences.zh: 所以这些效应是否真实很重要，而我们复现失败了。

sentences.en: But the attitude was, no, no, no, we don't publish replications.
sentences.zh: 但他们的态度是，不，不，不，我们不发表复现研究。

sentences.en: We were a bit cross about that, but we tried two other high-impact journals and got the same treatment.
sentences.zh: 我们对此有点生气，但我们尝试了另外两本高影响力的期刊，结果受到了同样的对待。

sentences.en: And again, we weren't saying, you know, you must publish this.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们并不是说，你们必须发表这个。

sentences.en: We were saying, send it out for peer review.
sentences.zh: 我们是在说，把它送去同行评审。

sentences.en: The British Journal of Psychology did send it out for peer review.
sentences.zh: 《英国心理学杂志》确实把它送去同行评审了。

sentences.en: One referee really loved the paper.
sentences.zh: 一位审稿人非常喜欢这篇论文。

sentences.en: The other one had concerns and wasn't too keen.
sentences.zh: 另一位有顾虑，不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: And we could recognise from what the concerns that were expressed were, we thought, we think we know who this referee is.
sentences.zh: 我们从表达的顾虑中认出了这位审稿人，我们认为我们知道他是谁。

sentences.en: We think it's a certain Daryl BEM.
sentences.zh: 我们认为是达里尔·贝姆本人。

sentences.en: And we asked him, and he confirmed it was him.
sentences.zh: 我们问了他，他证实确实是他。

sentences.en: So clearly, there's a conflict of interest there.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，那里存在利益冲突。

sentences.en: Yeah, how is that even possible, that the editor would use him as a referee?
sentences.zh: 是啊，编辑怎么会用他作为审稿人呢？这怎么可能？

sentences.en: That's what happened.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: So again, we said, well, you know, send it out for a third reviewer.
sentences.zh: 所以我们再次说，好吧，送给第三位审稿人看看。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: Long story short, we published it in PLOS One, which, as you'll know, is an open access journal,
sentences.zh: 长话短说，我们在《PLOS One》上发表了它，如你所知，这是一本开放获取期刊，

sentences.en: which turned out to be a good move, because at one point, we were getting like a thousand views a day, which is amazing for a scientific paper.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这是一个明智之举，因为有一段时间，我们每天获得大约一千次浏览，这对于科学论文来说是惊人的。

sentences.en: And it also fed into the ongoing discussions and debate about the replication crisis in psychology.
sentences.zh: 它也助推了关于心理学复现危机的持续讨论和辩论。

sentences.en: Because this was a situation where I say the paper had gone through the normal process of being reviewed and so on and so forth, and it had been published.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个我所说的论文已经通过了正常的评审过程等等，并且已经发表的情况。

sentences.en: Now, some people took the attitude of, well, the results can't possibly be true.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人采取的态度是，结果不可能正确。

sentences.en: Therefore, how could this happen?
sentences.zh: 那么，这怎么可能发生呢？

sentences.en: There's something wrong with the whole process, the whole kind of scientific publication.
sentences.zh: 整个过程，整个科学出版过程都有问题。

sentences.en: Others were kind of more open-minded about whether possibly the results might be true or not.
sentences.zh: 其他人则对结果是否可能正确持更开放的态度。

sentences.en: But I think what it did, it made me think long and hard about the ways in which spurious results may end up being published and the kind of pressures that are on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它所做的是，让我深入思考了虚假结果最终可能被发表的方式，以及所面临的压力。

sentences.en: And now, you know, the debate has kind of advanced to the extent that we all recognise that what we might call questionable research practices,
sentences.zh: 现在，辩论已经发展到我们都认识到所谓的“可疑研究实践”的程度，

sentences.en: not out-and-out fraud, much more subtle than that, but just kind of giving yourself the benefit of the doubt,
sentences.zh: 不是彻底的欺诈，比那微妙得多，只是给自己找借口，

sentences.en: knowing that you've got to get an effect that's just below that 0.05 level of significance, otherwise the editors won't look at it.
sentences.zh: 知道你必须得到一个刚好低于0.05显著性水平的效应，否则编辑就不会看它。

sentences.en: Then it kind of really highlighted how those issues can basically distort what ends up being published, and maybe particularly in what we would think of as the top journals,
sentences.zh: 这确实突显了这些问题如何从根本上扭曲最终发表的内容，也许特别是在我们认为的顶尖期刊中，

sentences.en: because they have a bias towards not only saying, well, we don't publish replications, because they're not interesting enough, we don't publish negative findings.
sentences.zh: 因为它们有一种偏见，不仅是说“我们不发表复现研究，因为它们不够有趣”，而且“我们不发表负面结果”。

sentences.en: And, you know, so all the negative findings and all the kind of just boring old replications just don't ever see the light of day.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有的负面结果和所有那些无聊的旧复现研究都永远见不到天日。

sentences.en: Or usually, in this case, as I say, we actually managed to kind of get it published.
sentences.zh: 或者通常情况下，就像我说的，我们实际上设法把它发表了。

sentences.en: Although that may be changing.
sentences.zh: 尽管这种情况可能正在改变。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there's more of a tendency now to...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为现在有一种更多的倾向去……

sentences.en: Oh, I think it definitely is, and I think it's a healthy thing.
sentences.zh: 哦，我认为绝对是这样，而且我认为这是一件健康的事情。

sentences.en: I think I'm kind of...
sentences.zh: 我想我有点……

sentences.en: You know, people talk about the kind of crisis in psychology.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论心理学的危机。

sentences.en: I just see it as a kind of healthy period of self-criticism.
sentences.zh: 我只是把它看作是一个健康的自我批评时期。

sentences.en: I must admit, I feel slightly guilty about it, because I can look back now and see papers that I have published in the past and think that probably wasn't a real effect.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我对此感到有点内疚，因为我现在回顾过去发表的论文，认为那可能不是一个真实的效应。

sentences.en: You know, things that I published and then tried to replicate myself and failed.
sentences.zh: 我发表的东西，然后自己尝试复现却失败了。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you even try to send off a paper that's about these failed replications, even though it's your own work, you know, you're trying to say,
sentences.zh: 如果你甚至尝试投递一篇关于这些失败复现的论文，即使是你自己的工作，你试图说，

sentences.en: no, I don't think that was real after all, you can't get it published.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为那毕竟是真的，你却无法发表它。

sentences.en: Whereas now, I think, as you say, things do seem to be in a direction where that's going to be easier to do.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我认为正如你所说，事情似乎正朝着更容易做到的方向发展。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So it's been a good outcome there, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个好的结果。

sentences.en: So I know you do a lot of writing for the general public about the work that you do.
sentences.zh: 我知道你为大众写了很多关于你所做工作的文章。

sentences.en: And what is one lesson that you'd want people to take away from your research?
sentences.zh: 你希望人们从你的研究中得到的一个教训是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I think what I just heard was part of it that science is evolving and that people should understand that, you know, we all need to keep an open mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我刚才听到的是其中的一部分，即科学在不断发展，人们应该明白，我们需要保持开放的心态。

sentences.en: But I mean, what would you say to just our average listener about what they should be thinking,
sentences.zh: 但我想问，对于我们的普通听众，你会对他们说他们应该思考什么，

sentences.en: say, about the paranormal, whether they believe in ghosts or think they've been abducted by aliens?
sentences.zh: 比如关于超自然现象，无论他们是相信鬼魂还是认为自己被外星人绑架了？

sentences.en: What would your best advice be?
sentences.zh: 你最好的建议是什么？

sentences.en: I suppose, maybe allow me kind of two or three nuggets here rather than just one.
sentences.zh: 我想，也许允许我提供两三个要点，而不是只有一个。

sentences.en: I mean, one thing would be that I think it's best to base your beliefs about the way the universe operates
sentences.zh: 我认为最好将你对宇宙运作方式的信念建立在坚实的实证证据上，

sentences.en: on kind of solid empirical evidence, preferably from well-controlled studies, rather than personal experience.
sentences.zh: 最好来自控制良好的研究，而不是个人经验。

sentences.en: Now, for most people, personal experience is the gold standard.
sentences.zh: 现在，对大多数人来说，个人经验是金标准。

sentences.en: You know, even still in the legal system, eyewitness testimony is given far more credence than it should be, given what we know about the way memory works.
sentences.zh: 即使在法律体系中，考虑到我们对记忆运作方式的了解，目击者证词仍然被赋予了远超其应有的信任。

sentences.en: So, you know, I think that would be one piece of advice that I think I'd like to pass on.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这将是我想要传达的一条建议。

sentences.en: And I think the other thing is kind of, as you've hinted at there, that science is not a kind of an established body of facts.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一件事是，正如你所暗示的那样，科学不是一套既定的事实。

sentences.en: It's something that evolves.
sentences.zh: 它是一个不断进化的事物。

sentences.en: And scientists will sometimes change their minds on issues.
sentences.zh: 科学家有时会改变对问题的看法。

sentences.en: And that's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事。

sentences.en: You know, it's a pity we don't have kind of more politicians who are able to do that.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我们没有更多能够做到这一点的政治家。

sentences.en: But because of the way political systems work, it's political suicide to change your mind on an issue.
sentences.zh: 但由于政治体系的运作方式，在问题上改变主意是政治自杀。

sentences.en: I mean, that's how we've ended up with Brexit and maybe how you ended up with Trump.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是我们最终导致英国脱欧，以及你们最终导致特朗普的原因。

sentences.en: But, you know, I mean, there's, I actually respect people greatly who kind of stand up and say, actually, I've realized I was wrong about that.
sentences.zh: 但我非常尊重那些站出来说“实际上，我意识到我在这方面错了”的人。

sentences.en: I think it's a good thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一件好事。

sentences.en: Whereas, you know, there is still this tendency for people to see that as being kind of wishy-washy and you can't make your mind up.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们仍然倾向于认为这是一种优柔寡断，无法下定决心。

sentences.en: I think that's a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个错误。

sentences.en: Well, this has been a fascinating exchange.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一次引人入胜的交流。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you joining us today, Dr. French.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天加入我们，弗伦奇博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我很享受这次谈话。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或 Apple、Stitcher、Spotify 或任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》的往期节目。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有评论或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 我们的声音编辑是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听。
